terms.meaning: server-side request forgery, where a server is tricked into requesting an internal address on an attacker's behalf
the internet's address book that turns a host name into numeric addresses
a numeric address for a machine on a network, in IPv4 or IPv6 form
a document file format whose text must be extracted before it can be read

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Loads the DNS lookup tool, the URL parser, and the retriever type this module implements.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed for lookups and to match the retriever contract.

sections.name: BLOCKED_HOSTNAMES
sections.title: Always-blocked host names
sections.what: Lists host names that are always refused, such as localhost and a cloud metadata host.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are common routes to internal services.
sections.watch_out: The list is short, so other internal names are not stopped by this list alone.

sections.name: BLOCKED_HOSTNAME_SUFFIXES
sections.title: Blocked host name endings
sections.what: Lists endings such as local and internal that are refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: these name internal networks.
sections.watch_out: Endings are matched in lower case after conversion, so a new ending must also be lower case.

sections.name: isBlockedHostname
sections.title: Checking a host name
sections.what: Checks a host name against the blocked names and endings, ignoring case.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick first check before any network lookup.
sections.watch_out: A public name can still point to a private address, which the address check must catch.

sections.name: isPrivateIP
sections.title: Checking whether an address is private
sections.what: Decides whether an address is private, loopback, link-local, or unspecified, for IPv4 and some IPv6.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops the server reaching internal machines.
sections.watch_out: The list is incomplete. Some reserved ranges are not covered.

sections.name: looksLikeIP
sections.title: Recognising an IP address
sections.what: Tells whether a text is already an IP address rather than a host name.
sections.why: Likely reason: an address can be checked directly with no lookup.
sections.watch_out: Any text with a colon is treated as IPv6, so unusual text with colons may be misread.

sections.name: resolveAndCheck
sections.title: Resolving and checking a host
sections.what: Looks up all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for a host. Refuses if any address is private, or if the host has none. Also sets the limits used later: redirects, page size, PDF size and timeout.
sections.why: The comments state that a host with no records is a dead link, not an attack, so it gets its own message.
sections.watch_out: The check happens at one moment, and the real request resolves the host again later. A changing DNS record could pass this check and then point somewhere else.

sections.name: isPdfUrl
sections.title: Recognising a PDF link
sections.what: Checks whether the path of a URL ends in pdf.
sections.why: Likely reason: decides PDF handling from the link alone.
sections.watch_out: A PDF behind a link without that ending is missed here. The content type check is a separate test.

sections.name: isPdfContentType
sections.title: Recognising a PDF response
sections.what: Checks whether the content type header says PDF.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the file type from the server's own statement.
sections.watch_out: Matching is loose, so a header that merely contains the words is treated as a PDF.

sections.name: extractPdfText
sections.title: Reading text from a PDF
sections.what: Reads text from PDF bytes, collapses spaces, and keeps at most 60,000 characters. On failure it logs a warning and returns empty text.
sections.why: The code notes the parser's interface changes between versions, so it tries two forms.
sections.watch_out: A failed read returns empty text, so a broken PDF looks like an empty document to callers.

summary: Downloads a web page or PDF only after checking that the address is public, and turns PDFs into plain text.
purpose: Stop the server from being tricked into reading internal machines or cloud metadata addresses.
why: The error messages name the protection: SSRF blocked for private targets. The DNS message separates dead links from attacks.
how: Checks the host name against a block list, resolves it to all its addresses, and refuses if any address is private. Also decides whether a link is a PDF and extracts text from PDF bytes. The fetch function itself is only partly included in this packet.
inputs: URLs and host names. PDF bytes when a PDF is being read.
outputs: Fetched content, extracted PDF text, or an error that says why a fetch was refused.
risks: The address is checked before the request, so the address could change in between. The list of private ranges is partial. A PDF read failure returns empty text silently.
debug: Error text names the reason: SSRF blocked or DNS unresolvable. Check the host name and its DNS records. For PDF problems, look for the PDF parse failed warning in the logs.
